Hence exact dimensions 0,1,2,4,6,9 for n=1,...,6. No extrapolation beyond six.

originality.rationale: Goldman--Rivest--Schapire 1993 studied exactly this comparator learning model and already established its Omega(n log n) qualitative hardness and counting upper bound; neither covers equality with floorlog2(n!) for each n up to six in the inspected Section 4.2. Johnson--Wickes 2021 concerns item-wise k!-pattern shattering, not binary pairwise adaptive shattering. Semantic searches in published mathematical records found no equivalent exact 512-leaf benchmark. Historical priority remains a real residual risk; the old qualitative gap and cardinality upper bound are not claimed as new. The 2021 mathematics-logic paper arXiv:2109.04805 proves equality for linear zero-set families, inapplicable to comparator families with a strict gap.
residual_risks: Other classic ranking-learning papers might determine these very small finite exact comparator-tree values using a different term than Littlestone dimension.
No exact formula beyond six labels is established; general growth and an unbounded gap were already in prior literature.
Historical access was incomplete for some older mathematical research records; no uniqueness inference is made from those gaps.

value.rationale: Whether the elementary hypothesis-count ceiling is actually achieved is a precise, motivated finite invariant for comparison prediction. A 512-leaf full mistake tree from only 720 orders is a nonroutine exact extremal certificate, and the full small-order cutoff identifies the first VC/Littlestone separation at four labels; these benchmarks calibrate exact online learning of total rankings. No general theorem or paper-sized result is required, and no artificial subfamily or arbitrary numerical parameter was selected. Results for n>6 remain open in this work.
